concept_name: Pure Rolling — v = Rω and the Contact Point at Rest
source_book: NCERT Class 11 Physics Ch.7 §7.14 (System of Particles and Rotational Motion — rolling motion) — table-of-contents scope only, teaching authored from first principles. The atomic idea: a rolling-without-slipping body ties its centre speed v to its turn rate omega through v = Rω, and the direct consequence is that the contact point is, at that instant, at rest — so the friction acting at a rolling contact is static, never kinetic. Does NOT cover the incline race or the shape factor I/mR² (deferred to rolling_on_incline), and does NOT cover rotational kinetic energy (deferred to rotational_work_energy). DC Pandey chapter table of contents consulted for scope only — no teaching method, example or figure imported; NCERT §7.14's slide-plus-spin decomposition is re-derived from first principles as STATE_4–STATE_6, not copied. Built on the newtons_laws_body field_3d engine, SEAM R (the bounded rotational extension), zero renderer edits.

real_world_anchor.primary: A bicycle wheel crosses the road exactly this way.
real_world_anchor.secondary: A braked, locked wheel leaves a skid mark; a rolling wheel leaves none.

omega0.name: starting spin omega0, decoupled from v
omega0.derived: v0 / R, recomputed live in STATE_8 whenever v0 or R changes and omega0 itself is not being dragged

k.name: moment-of-inertia coefficient, I = k m R squared, uniform disc

theta_deg.name: incline angle, this concept is flat

constraints: v = R*omega holds identically for a rolling body (STATE_1, STATE_2, STATE_6, STATE_3 phase B) — it is NOT true by construction in STATE_4 (pure slide, omega held 0) or STATE_5 (pure spin, v held 0); those two are the ingredients whose sum, in STATE_6, satisfies v = R*omega.
Contact-point speed |v - omega*R| = 0 exactly whenever v = R*omega holds; nonzero only during a genuinely sliding contact (STATE_3 phase A, rotation locked; STATE_7 pre-capture).

k = I/(m R^2) = 0.5 for every wheel body in this concept — the wheel is modelled as a uniform disc. k is never rendered on canvas anywhere (do-not-prespoil — k is rolling_on_incline's authored reveal).
Kinetic friction f_k = mu_k*m*g acts only while the contact point is genuinely sliding; never on a body already satisfying v = R*omega.
theta = 0 (flat track) throughout — no incline forms anywhere in this concept, contrast with rolling_on_incline.
The revolution-marks primitive is a pure function of turn count (s_n = x0 - n*2*PI*R), never of authored milliseconds — a mark stamp fires when one more completed turn is satisfied.
capture_time_s and capture_speed are closed-form results of Newton's second law plus the torque-angular-acceleration relation for a uniform disc, never a per-frame latch.

aha_moment.statement: The point where a rolling wheel touches the road is, at that instant, not moving.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: The rim dot comes to rest at each ground touch while the centre arrow keeps reading 0.60 m/s and the contact marker holds 0.00 m/s.

STATE_1.title: One turn, one circumference
STATE_1.motion_archetype: reveal-build (declared contrast pair of STATE_6 — reads v = Rω from the ground)

scene_composition.text: The wheel rolls forward: its centre speed and its turn rate are locked together
each completed turn puts exactly one circumference, 2 pi R, of road behind the wheel
a bicycle wheel crosses the road exactly this way

tts_sentences.text_en: The wheel's centre moves along the road at speed v.
Its turn rate, omega, angular velocity, counts the angle turned each second.
Each completed turn puts exactly one circumference, 2πR, of road behind it.
So the two are locked: speed v equals R times omega.
A bicycle wheel crosses the road exactly this way.

STATE_2.title: The contact point is at rest

scene_composition.text: Watch the point where the wheel touches the road
the marked rim point comes to a stop at every ground touch, while the centre keeps moving
the contact reading stays at 0.00 metres per second

tts_sentences.text_en: Watch the point where the wheel touches the road — the centre above it moves forward at speed v.
But the bottom point comes to rest at every touch, not moving forward at all.
Its speed reads zero exactly there, while the centre keeps moving.

misconception_watch.belief: Every point of the wheel moves at the wheel's speed — the bottom slides along the road.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The rim dot comes to rest at each ground touch while the centre arrow keeps reading 0.60 m/s and the contact marker reads 0.00 m/s.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: The turn carries the bottom point backward at exactly the speed the wheel moves forward, so at the ground the two cancel to zero.

scene_composition.text: A locked wheel skids in, slows and stops, leaving a mark
that skidding wheel is gone; the same wheel now rolls instead, crossing at a steady speed with no mark
a braked, locked wheel leaves a skid mark; a rolling wheel leaves none

tts_sentences.text_en: A locked wheel skids in, slows, and stops, leaving a skid mark.
That skidding wheel is gone; the same wheel now rolls instead.
It crosses at a steady speed, leaving no mark: the contact point is not sliding, so friction is zero.
A braked, locked wheel leaves a skid mark; a rolling wheel leaves none.

misconception_watch.belief: A rolling wheel slides against the road, so its friction is kinetic and always slows it down.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The locked wheel skids by itself first, slowing down and leaving a mark, then stops. The same wheel then rolls across at a steady speed with no mark and a friction reading of 0.00 newtons.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Kinetic friction needs a sliding contact; a rolling contact point is at rest, so only static friction can ever act there — and here even that reads zero.

scene_composition.text: This wheel slides without turning at all
the top, the centre and the bottom all move at the same speed
no turning means every point of the wheel moves the same way

tts_sentences.text_en: This wheel slides without turning at all.
The top of the wheel moves at speed v.
So does the centre.
So does the bottom — every point, the same speed.

STATE_5.title: Spin in place: centre at rest

scene_composition.text: This wheel spins on the spot, its centre fixed
the top of the rim moves forward, the bottom moves backward, equally fast
only the centre stays still

tts_sentences.text_en: This wheel spins on the spot.
The top of the rim moves forward.
The bottom of the rim moves backward, equally fast.
Only the centre stays still.

STATE_6.title: Slide plus spin makes rolling
STATE_6.motion_archetype: reveal-build (declared contrast pair of STATE_1 — reads v = Rω from the points)

scene_composition.text: This wheel is truly rolling: sliding and spinning add together
at the top the two add to two v, at the centre only sliding remains, at the contact they cancel to zero
v + R omega = 2v,  v − R omega = 0

tts_sentences.text_en: This wheel is truly rolling: sliding and spinning add together.
At the top, the two add: speed v plus R omega makes two v.
At the centre, only sliding remains: speed v alone.
At the contact point, the two cancel: speed v minus R omega equals zero.

scene_composition.text: This wheel starts moving but not spinning
friction's turning effect on the rim speeds the spin up while it slows the slide
speed v and R omega converge, and the moment they meet, it rolls

tts_sentences.text_en: This wheel starts moving but not spinning; it slides at first.
Friction's turning effect on the rim speeds the spin up — a torque doing to turn rate omega what a force does to speed v.
Speed v and R omega converge, and the moment they meet, it rolls.

scene_composition.text: Change every value yourself
drag speed, radius, starting spin and friction — watch the wheel respond
v = R omega

tts_sentences.text_en: Now change the wheel's speed, radius, starting spin, and friction yourself, and watch it roll.

regeneration_variants.label: A Car Tyre on the Highway
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A car tyre rolling along a highway shows the same locked relation between how fast the car travels and how fast the tyre turns.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Identical rolling condition: v = Rω, and the same contact-point-at-rest result — only the labelled world changes from a bicycle wheel to a car tyre.
regeneration_variants.scene_hint: Same single-wheel rig on the same flat track — only the labelled object changes from a bicycle wheel to a car tyre.

regeneration_variants.label: A Shopping Cart Wheel Crossing a Floor
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A shopping cart's wheel rolling across a flat floor ties its travel speed to its turn rate the same way any rolling wheel does.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Same rolling condition and the same contact-at-rest result — only the labelled object changes from a bicycle wheel to a cart wheel.
regeneration_variants.scene_hint: Same single-wheel rig, same flat floor — only the labelled object changes.

assessment.mastery_definition: A student who has mastered this concept can state v = Rω for a rolling wheel, explain why a rolling contact point is instantaneously at rest, identify that a rolling contact never involves kinetic friction, decompose a rolling wheel's point speeds into 0/v/2v, and predict how a wheel launched without spin evolves into rolling under kinetic friction.

questions.stem: A wheel of radius R rolls without slipping and its centre moves at speed v. What is the wheel's angular speed, omega?

distractor_misconceptions.A: Believes multiplying converts linear speed to angular speed instead of dividing by radius.
distractor_misconceptions.B: Inverts the rolling relation, swapping which quantity is divided by which.
distractor_misconceptions.D: Does not know rolling ties translation and rotation together at all.

questions.parallel_form_stem: A ball of radius r rolls without slipping and its centre moves at speed v0. Which expression gives its angular speed?

questions.stem: A wheel rolls without slipping along a road. What is the speed of the point of the wheel touching the road, at that instant?

options.B: Equal to v, the same as the centre

distractor_misconceptions.B: Assumes every point of a rigid wheel must move at the same speed as the centre.
distractor_misconceptions.C: Confuses the ground contact point with the top point, which does move at 2v.
distractor_misconceptions.D: Believes mass affects a purely kinematic velocity relation.

questions.parallel_form_stem: A ball rolls without slipping across a floor. At the instant a marked point on its surface touches the floor, how fast is that point moving?

questions.stem: A wheel rolls without slipping at constant speed on a level road. What type of friction, if any, acts at the contact point?

options.C: Static friction equal to the wheel's full weight
options.D: None — the contact point is not sliding, so kinetic friction is zero

distractor_misconceptions.A: Assumes rolling contact behaves like sliding contact and always loses energy to kinetic friction.
distractor_misconceptions.B: Invents a friction force in the direction of motion with no physical cause.
distractor_misconceptions.C: Confuses the normal force, which does equal the weight here, with friction.

questions.tested_idea: rolling contact means no kinetic friction
questions.parallel_form_stem: A ball rolls without slipping at a steady speed across a level floor. What friction acts where it touches the floor?

questions.stem: A wheel slides along a road with its rotation completely locked — it does not spin at all. How does the speed of its top point compare with its bottom point?

options.A: The top point moves faster than the bottom point
options.B: They are equal — every point moves at the same speed as the centre
options.C: The bottom point moves faster than the top point

distractor_misconceptions.A: Assumes rotation causes the usual top-faster-than-bottom pattern even though rotation is locked here.
distractor_misconceptions.C: Reverses the usual rolling pattern without checking that there is no rotation in this case.
distractor_misconceptions.D: Imports the rolling wheel's zero-contact-speed result into a case where the wheel is not rolling at all.

questions.tested_idea: pure translation gives every point the same speed
questions.parallel_form_stem: A crate slides across an icy floor without tipping or turning. How does the speed of its top edge compare with its bottom edge?

questions.stem: A wheel spins in place with its centre fixed — it does not translate at all. How does the speed of its top point compare with its bottom point?

options.A: Equal in speed, opposite in direction
options.D: The bottom point moves faster because it is closer to the ground

distractor_misconceptions.B: Ignores that opposite sides of a spinning wheel move in opposite directions.
distractor_misconceptions.C: Confuses this case with the rolling wheel's contact point, which is at rest only when the wheel also translates.
distractor_misconceptions.D: Invents a dependence on distance to the ground that pure rotation does not have.

questions.tested_idea: pure rotation gives equal and opposite rim speeds, centre at rest
questions.parallel_form_stem: A fan blade tip spins about a fixed centre. How do the speeds of two points on opposite sides of the centre compare?

questions.stem: For a wheel rolling without slipping at centre speed v, what is the speed of the point at the very top of the wheel?

distractor_misconceptions.A: Stops at the centre's speed, missing that the spin adds to it at the top.
distractor_misconceptions.B: Confuses the top point with the contact point at the bottom, which is the one that reads zero.
distractor_misconceptions.D: Guesses the spin halves the speed instead of adding an equal amount.

questions.tested_idea: rolling = slide plus spin; top point speed is v + Rω = 2v
questions.parallel_form_stem: A ball rolls without slipping at centre speed v0. How fast is the point at the very top of the ball moving?

questions.stem: A wheel is launched moving forward with no spin at all on a rough level floor. What happens as kinetic friction acts?

options.A: It keeps sliding forever at its launch speed, since friction cannot start a spin
options.B: Its forward speed decreases and its spin speed increases, until the two match and it starts rolling
options.C: It stops completely and never rolls
options.D: It speeds up because friction pushes it forward

distractor_misconceptions.A: Believes friction can only oppose translation and cannot also apply a spinning torque.
distractor_misconceptions.C: Assumes friction always brings a slipping body fully to rest rather than to a nonzero rolling speed.
distractor_misconceptions.D: Reverses the direction kinetic friction acts on a forward-sliding contact.

questions.tested_idea: slipping converges to rolling under kinetic friction
questions.parallel_form_stem: A ball is launched moving forward with no spin on a rough floor. What eventually happens to its motion?

STATE_1.label: The wheel rolls at v = 0.90 m/s; each completed turn advances it exactly one circumference, 2πR = 1.57 m; v and Rω sit equal
STATE_1.caption: One turn, one circumference

STATE_2.label: Slow roll at 0.60 m/s: the marked rim point comes to rest at each ground touch, while the centre arrow reads 0.60 m/s and the contact marker holds 0.00 m/s
STATE_2.caption: Contact point speed: zero

STATE_3.label: A locked wheel skids in at 2.0 m/s, slows at 1.96 m/s squared and stops, leaving a mark; the same wheel then rolls across at a steady 2.0 m/s with no mark and f = 0.00 N
STATE_3.caption: Skid slows; roll does not

STATE_4.label: The wheel slides at 1.0 m/s with its spokes visibly not turning: the top, centre and bottom all read exactly the same speed
STATE_4.caption: Sliding: one speed everywhere

STATE_5.label: The wheel spins on the spot at omega = 4.0 rad/s: the top of the rim moves forward, the bottom moves backward equally fast, and the centre stays at rest
STATE_5.caption: Rim turns, centre stays

STATE_6.label: The wheel truly rolls, v = 1.00 m/s and v = Rω: the top reads 2.00 m/s (2v), the centre 1.00 m/s (v), and the contact 0.00 m/s (v − Rω)
STATE_6.caption: Slide plus spin: roll

STATE_7.label: The wheel launches at v0 with no spin: kinetic friction slows v and spins omega up until they meet at capture, then it rolls with f = 0.00 N
STATE_7.caption: Sliding becomes rolling

STATE_8.label: Explore: change speed, radius, starting spin and friction — the wheel rolls or slides as the numbers dictate
STATE_8.caption: All controls live
